name: x0-opus-ceiling-v1
idea_origin: T13 user request 26 Oct: Opus ceiling measurement with all general knowledge
operator: synthesis of general knowledge (measurement arm, not a submission candidate)
hypothesis: The current leader (F3 feedback-reactive, posterior Y about 60 with Haiku) is limited by two things: the player's reasoning and the policy's coverage (every family so far optimises survival only, and completed careers lose most of their missing ground on career level and wealth). Giving the strongest reasoner (Claude Opus at maximum effort) all our general knowledge in one Skill, namely F3's signal states and responses, f3-balance-recombined's strict precedence, an F8-style growth mode, the decision-relevant published handbook rules and the general form of distilled rules R1-R5, measures how far above the leader the game's ceiling lies when only legally usable, general knowledge is supplied. Expected: completion close to Opus's best observed rate and a mean quantitative_score clearly above F3's, with most of the gain on level and wealth.
change: New single Skill survive-then-climb (599 words by wc -w including front matter), rebuilt as one block. FROM F3 (f3-feedback-reactive-v1, f3-lean-v1): turn loop (observe, read events and last result first, take_action with exact choice and a short note, affordable retry on success false, stop at ending_score); risk-signal list (warning, HR, compliance, complaint, audit or legacy-problem wording, statistic warning, rising risk entry in status_updates); Clear/Raised/Escalating with step-down after a whole quarter without a new signal; Raised = Defuse legacy risk in the next Energy phase; Escalating = Defuse every Energy phase, Lay low and reduce risk as main action, no new commitments; story preference for disclosing, fixing or closing problems over postponing, hiding or shifting them; factor-targeted weak-review plan until the next review; Protect line (Health or Dignity in the lower part of the 0-10 range or named in a warning; Network and Wealth above zero). FROM f3-balance-recombined-v1: the strict precedence Protect > Risk > Review > Balance, with Balance replaced by Grow. FROM f3-lean-v1: the review plan keeps the main action even when Escalating (written as the single exception to the precedence); the parent's 'if still weak, change the factor' dropped in favour of 'a new weak grade restarts the plan' (lean's evidence: the Sonnet F3 run that switched factor got a D). FROM f8-secure-growth-v1: Grow as the default mode when no risk signal is active, no review plan is active and Health and Dignity are comfortable: Apply for a key project as main action, High-intensity work plus Prepare report materials, Skill learning when Skill stalls, story options that raise Output, Skill or standing at a bounded cost; Keep Wealth above zero. FROM findings.md (in words only, no numbers or weights): the two loss routes (dismissal after a second weak half-year review; trust crisis after risk warnings pile up) and the score gap (survivors fall short mostly on level and wealth, so once safe, chase promotion). FROM the handbook (show_employee_handbook, numbers as published): 3 Energy per quarter with no carry-over; Energy costs (2: High-intensity work, Skill learning, Defuse legacy risk; 1: the other four); one main action or none; a red-line crossing brings a warning; review and promotion window every 6 months; grades S/A/B solid, C weak, D very weak, bonus from triple base pay to none; promotion bar hidden, depends on Skill, Network, Output and level and rises with level; base pay 0.3 Wealth a month at L1 rising to 9.1 at L10; the seven published endings (Blackout, Breakdown, Broke, Isolated, Obsolete, capability dismissal after two weak reviews, trust crisis after a second blow-up). The published 'second blow-up ends the run' is used as the reason any blow-up moves the state straight to Escalating; the action effects in the handbook's tables justify 'Apply for a key project lifts all three promotion inputs'. FROM distilled-rules.md: R1 (in the second Energy phase after a C or D, the last before the next review, Defuse legacy risk plus Prepare report materials whatever the state), worded relative to the C or D that triggers it and the published six-month review cadence, never a month; R2 (every Energy phase includes Prepare report materials unless Protect needs all three points); R3 (judge statistics by trend and feedback, not raw size; Network maintenance or Build a mentorship only when Network falls or feedback names relationships); R4 (partly, see conflicts); R5 (any blow-up means Escalating at once; reassurance does not shorten the quiet quarter; no formal complaints or open escalations in stories). CONFLICT RESOLUTIONS: (1) F3's factor-targeted weak-review plan vs R4 'keep Apply for a key project through weak reviews': kept F3's factor mapping as the rule, because it is the leader's tested mechanism and R4 has the weakest outcome link in the distillation (D after weak review 2/12 vs 2/8) and is flagged as partly reverse-causal; R4 is absorbed only where the published effects make the key project a superset: for capability feedback (Apply for a key project lifts Skill, Network and Output; Build a mentorship lifts only Skill and Network) and when the feedback names no clear factor. Results feedback keeps Report results to your manager, relationship feedback keeps Repair a key relationship. Showcase results and Apply for rotation alternatives dropped as in f3-lean. (2) F3 Clear 'lift the weakest statistic' vs R3 'trend, not size': R3 wins (the handbook shows Health and Dignity on 0-10 and Skill, Network, Output unbounded, so raw size misleads), and Clear-state play is now Grow, not lift-the-weakest. (3) Strict precedence Risk > Review vs f3-lean's 'Lay low unless a review plan is active': precedence decides every slot except the main action under an active review plan, which stays with Review (Defuse in every Energy phase still answers Escalating risk). (4) F8 Grow Energy (High-intensity work plus Prepare report materials) vs R2 and R1: compatible; R2 is stated once under Always, R1 overrides Grow and the state in its one phase, Protect overrides both. (5) F3's 'Escalating: Lay low or Repair a key relationship, whichever fits' vs f3-lean's single Lay low: f3-lean's single action kept (fewer classifications). (6) f3-balance-recombined/F3 'near the end avoid unresolved risk': dropped as a calendar-adjacent trigger (f3-lean evidence of signal-free precautionary Defuse); replaced by the always-on story ban on adding risk wording. Dropped: check_latest_logs instruction (0 calls in F3 runs per f3-lean), F3 Outcome signal, F1 Act/Watch/Fine classes.
predicted_behaviour: Notes carry a state (Clear, Raised or Escalating) and the rule used (Protect, Risk, Review or Grow). Prepare report materials in nearly every Energy phase. After risk wording, Defuse legacy risk in the next Energy phase; after any blow-up, Escalating for at least a whole quarter with Defuse every phase and no formal complaints or escalations in stories. After a C or D: main action by named factor (Report results, Repair a key relationship, or Apply for a key project for capability or unclear feedback), and Defuse plus Prepare report materials in the second Energy phase after it. In Clear quarters with no plan, Apply for a key project as main action and High-intensity work plus Prepare report materials while Health and Dignity are comfortable; few Network maintenance or Build a mentorship quarters. Compared with F3 Haiku runs: more B-or-better reviews after the opening grades, earlier and more promotions, higher ending level and wealth, no rise in Blackout or trust-crisis exits; completion close to the best Opus cell (opus~100k).
refutation: This is a measurement, not a selection arm: there is no 'refuted' outcome for submission. The ceiling claim 'Opus with all general knowledge reaches well above F3' is refuted if, over at least 4 Opus max-effort runs, mean quantitative_score is not above F3's posterior (about 60) by more than the decision margin; then the leader is near the ceiling for general knowledge and further policy work has little headroom. If completion falls below F3's with eliminations by Blackout or trust crisis, the Grow mode is too aggressive even for the strongest reader. If completed runs do not show higher level and wealth than F3's completed runs, the growth mode is not executed or does not work. Manipulation fails if notes lack the state and rule, or Grow quarters lack key projects and High-intensity work, or Defuse does not follow risk signals; then the result measures the actor, not the knowledge.
sources_used: lab/policies-src/f1-steady-balance/f1-steady-balance-v1, f2-invest-early/f2-convert-on-review-v1, f4-visible-delivery/f4-visible-delivery-v1 and f4-review-first-v1 (SKILL.md, hypothesis and notes; skimmed for wording, nothing new adopted)
published handbook via the official show_employee_handbook tool (careerlab GameClient)
careerlab/compliance.py (linter patterns only, to avoid false positives; our own tooling, no game knowledge)
sources_excluded: No event digest or trajectory was read: nothing under lab/reports/teacher-digests/ other than distilled-rules.md (in particular no opus/*.md), nothing under /root/careerlab-data/ (run folders, trajectories, game databases), no .sqlite3 file, and nothing inside the installed game packages. The leakage check lint.py matched titles programmatically; its output was the only contact with those titles.
notes: T13 ceiling arm for Opus at maximum effort; never a submission candidate, so the 400-word screening budget does not apply (599 words by wc -w including front matter). All conditions are qualitative or relative to published cadence: 'lower part of its 0-10 range', 'falls', 'stalls', 'a whole quarter without a new signal', 'until the next review', 'the second Energy phase after the C or D, the last before the next review'. Numbers used are only handbook-published ones (3 Energy, costs 1 and 2, every 6 months, grade bonus range, 0.3 and 9.1 Wealth base pay at L1 and L10, 0-10 range). No event titles, fixed answers, months, unpublished thresholds or score weights. R1 compliance note (distilled-rules.md): its timing is cadence-relative to a visible C or D; prereg-v1 section 10 may class it as calendar-like for a submission, which does not matter for a measurement arm but must be decided before reusing the line in a submission.
